intent: I live in Shaw Heights with a Westminster address and Westminster water. Do Westminster's artificial turf rules decide where turf can go in my yard, and if not, whose rules do, and who do I ask?
distinctValue: Shaw Heights is unincorporated Adams County, and Westminster's own 2025 and 2026 water rate sheets bill it as a separate customer class (Shaw Heights 1.10 against In City 1.0 and Out of City 1.25). So the Westminster landscape regulations that the Westminster page presents (turf only in yard areas not adjacent to a street, park or open space) are city rules that do not govern the lot. What governs it is the Adams County Development Standards and Regulations: 4-19-04-01 says no artificial turf shall be used as a landscape material, but 4-19-02 applies that section only to new development and to existing development needing a change in use permit, so a re-landscape of an existing house is an open question for the county's Planner of the Day, with a zoning verification application as the formal route. Time-sensitive and local only to unincorporated Adams County: the Development Standards Overhaul draft (case PRC2026-00016) keeps the turf line, adds a functional-use test, says Div. 4-04 generally applies to new construction, and goes to hearings on 22 October and 17 November 2026 with a 1 January 2027 start if adopted. Also local: Shaw Heights' own Westminster water tiers, sewer billed on average winter use, and USDA soil at the centre of the CDP (Platner loam, 3 to 5 percent slopes, smectitic, clay reaching 40% with linear extensibility of 7.3).

sources.label: Shaw Heights, Colorado (Wikipedia)
supports: Shaw Heights is an unincorporated community and a census-designated place (CDP) located in and governed by Adams County, Colorado, United States.
The Westminster post office (Zip code 80031) serves the area.

sources.label: City of Westminster: Landscape Regulations 2004 (PDF)
supports: These Landscape Regulations have been adopted by the Westminster City Council. All areas to be landscaped shall incorporate the requirements herein. Enforcement of the regulations shall be as provided in Section 1-8-1 of the Westminster Municipal Code.
The use of artificial turf is generally prohibited, except for use in single-family detached or duplex lot yard areas not adjacent to a street, or public or private park or open space.

sources.label: Adams County Development Standards and Regulations, Chapter 4, October 1, 2024 (PDF)
supports: Chapter 4—Design Requirements and Performance Standards, October 1, 2024

4-19-04-01 LANDSCAPE MATERIALS: No artificial trees, plants, or turf shall be used as a landscape material. If an applicant is interested in using artificial turf in their development, they shall meet the minimum standards for required plant materials and submit a request for an alternative turf design with drainage specifications to the Director of Community and Economic Development.

4-19-02 APPLICABILITY: The provisions of this article shall apply to development, which meets one (1) of the following and is not exempt: 1. All new development which has not applied for a building permit before the effective date of this Section; or 2. Existing development which requires a change in use permit as determined within the Change in Use Section of Chapter 4.

4-02-01 CHANGE IN USE: A change in use of property occurs whenever the essential character or nature of the activity conducted on a lot changes. All changes in use require zoning review and building permit approval.

sources.label: Adams County: DRAFT Development Standards and Regulations, Chapter 4 (PDF)
supports: For example, Div. 4-04, Landscaping and Buffering, generally applies to new construction; however, some provisions of the Division apply to nonresidential development that do not apply to all residential types of development.

Landscape Materials. No artificial trees, plants, or turfgrass shall be used as a landscape material. If an applicant is interested in using artificial turf in their development, they shall meet the minimum standards for required plant materials, demonstrate a functional use for the artificial turf, and submit a request for an alternative turf design with drainage specifications to the Director of Community and Economic Development.

No person shall install, plant, or place, or allow any person to install, plant, or place, any nonfunctional turfgrass, nonfunctional artificial turf, or invasive plant species, as part of a new development project or redevelopment project, on any portion of applicable property.

For purposes of this prohibition, "applicable property" means: (A) Commercial, institutional, or industrial property as defined in C.R.S. § 37-60-135(2)(b); (B) Common interest community property as defined in C.R.S. § 38-33.3-103(8); or (C) A street right-of-way, parking lot, median, or transportation corridor.
On and after January 1, 2028, no person shall install, plant, or place ... (D) A multifamily residential housing premises property that includes more than twelve dwelling units.

The City of Westminster will enact a Drought Watch effective Wednesday, April 15, in response to Colorado's dry conditions and record-low snowpack, and its impact to the City's projected water supply.
Mandatory watering restrictions are not currently in place.
Limit lawn watering to no more than three days per week. Water before 10 am or after 6 pm to reduce evaporation.
During the summer, three out of every four gallons of water are used to water a home's lawn and garden
